Read literally, MAE(BCA z vs BCA v) minus MAE(native q vs native v) is positive when BCA's error is larger. 3.8 passes when "the decrease exceeds 3.6", so the literal formula passes when BCA is worse by more than the practical effect size. A decrease in BCA's error relative to native is native minus BCA. Two readers could compute opposite signs and reach opposite verdicts from the same data.

DECISION_BLOCK.md:107 "Pass. For S of 4 or fewer: the decrease exceeds 3.6 in every seed."
Worked example: MAE_BCA = 50, MAE_native = 40. The literal 3.5 formula gives 50 - 40 = +10 (> 0, so a Pass if 3.6 < 10), yet BCA is worse. The intended decrease is 40 - 50 = -10.

findings.title: Pass, Fail and Inconclusive overlap, and a failed 7.5 leaves Pass possible but Fail impossible
findings.problem: Pass has no gate condition. Fail requires every section-7 gate to pass, including 7.5, the free-policy entry gate. Inconclusive applies when any gate fails. So: (a) the pass rule met with 7.5 failed is both Pass and Inconclusive; (b) all gates passed, the learning check failed and the pass rule unmet is both Fail and Inconclusive. 7.6 says that when 7.5 fails, forced-probe accuracy (which is exactly the primary) may still be reported. 8.3 gates the primary only on step 2 passing "for the primary stratum", and 7.5 is not a property of that stratum. With 7.5 failed, the primary can therefore be computed and can reach Pass, but it can never reach Fail. This is an outcome asymmetry that favors BCA. A 7.5 failure is the likely case: the development actor had 0 of 128 commands in the band.

findings.title: The S of 5 or more test is not specified, and some combinations the form allows can never pass
findings.problem: The form does not say what the sign test or paired t tests: the sign of D greater than 0, or D greater than the practical size in 3.6. It gives no rule for ties. The smallest achievable one-sided sign-test p is 2^-S. At S = 5 it is 0.03125, so any chosen alpha below that (for example 0.025 or 0.01) makes Pass impossible, and the form does not warn about this. At alpha 0.05 the sign test needs every seed positive for S = 5, 6 and 7, so a smaller "at least ___ of S" count is ineffective. The user could also enter a count greater than S. If 9.9 "shared across seeds" is chosen, the seed-level test treats seeds as independent, which v2 says they then are not.

findings.title: The primary mixes the adjusted BCA score with the raw native critic, and the different Q^pi references are not disclosed
findings.problem: v2 keeps the same-critic adjustment panel (q against z) separate from the trained-critic panel. Native also has shadow auxiliary and calibration work, so a native z exists. The development critic overestimates in-band high-load commands by tens of units, so subtracting a nonnegative kappa*U lowers BCA's MAE mechanically even if BCA's trained critic is no better. This choice therefore favors BCA. The form also does not tell the user that the two errors are measured against different continuation policies, which v2 says is "not a correction against one common target".
